newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police foil guerrilla gun attack.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police foil guerrilla gun attack.

text.p: Northern Irish police foiled a guerrilla ambush and arrested one person in south Belfast on Wednesday, a police spokesman said.
Police seized two fully-loaded assault rifles after raiding a house that they suspected had been taken over by armed men, security sources said.
"It is clear that this was a determined attempt by terrorists to kill or maim," Belfast police commander Bill Stewart said in a statement.
"We consider the recovery of two AK 47 rifles which were fully loaded and ready for use to be very significant indeed. It is clear lives have been saved today..."
He said that one person had been arrested for questioning and that a follow-up security operation was under way.
The attempted ambush was in Black's Road, near Dunmurry, which is often used by patrolling British army vehicles en route to a nearby Irish nationalist area.

Police did not indicate which of the British province's armed groups were behind the attack but security analysts said AK 47s are a favourite weapon of Irish Republican Army guerrillas, who have been waging a long campaign against British rule.
Police said that they were alerted to the incident by "suspicious activity" in the area.

The incident happened just hours ahead of a major parliamentary statement by British Prime Minister, Tony Blair, aimed at getting the IRA to call an end to its violence to win a political voice in peace talks.
Blair was due to tell the British House of Commons of Anglo-Irish plans for resolving a long-running deadlock over how to achieve IRA disarmament if the guerrillas called a truce.
